title: Deliver Me, O Lord

questions.question: In my distress I called to the Lord, and he did what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 120:1 (ESV): "In my distress I called to the Lord, and he answered me."

questions.question: Deliver me, O Lord, from lying lips, from a deceitful what?
What shall be given to you, and what more shall be done to you, you deceitful tongue? A warrior's sharp what?
With glowing coals of what tree?
questions.explanation: Psalm 120:4 (ESV): "...with glowing coals of the broom tree!"

questions.question: Woe to me, that I sojourn in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 120:5 (ESV): "...that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!"

questions.question: Too long have I had my dwelling among those who hate what?
I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 120:7 (ESV): "I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war!"

questions.question: This Psalm is the first of the Songs of what?
What characterizes the tongue in verse 2?
What characterizes the lips in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Psalm 120:2 (ESV): "Deliver me, O Lord, from lying lips,"

questions.question: Meshech and Kedar represent what?
questions.explanation: They represent distant and hostile people.

questions.question: The mention of "glowing coals of the broom tree" implies what?
questions.explanation: Broom wood makes charcoal that retains heat for a long time, symbolizing severe judgment.

questions.question: How many Songs of Ascents are there?
Who is the author of Psalm 120?
questions.explanation: The title does not attribute it to anyone.

questions.question: What does the psalmist seek in verse 2?

key_verse_text: In my distress I called to the Lord, and he answered me.
